📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Recent findings suggest that lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

According to recent reports, “I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo stated: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Looks to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

In a recent development, “There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” notes Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”.

Though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

“It really is about the hooligan era,” states a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”.

Sources indicate that jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd.

There have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

According to recent reports, at the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at Fresh Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”.

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

The hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG.

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police mentioned that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Industry observers note that just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means….

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno stated: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

Recent findings suggest that on potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”.

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn.

#westham on the way to #millwall via #london bridge #whufc #coyi pic.twitter.com/HrWgJ6UtJY.

Industry observers note that riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

The game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

It has been revealed that “I don’t want to be better! I want to be …!” She choked on a sob and abruptly stood, banging her knee against the desk and wincing.

I held up a hand. “It’s all right, Joan.”.

“You just …” she sobbed, “… think I’m being … st-stupid …”.

Sources indicate that “No. I think you’re being human.”.

It has been revealed that she laughed — one quick snort — then wiped at her eyes with the back of a sleeve. “Sorry.”.

“Nothing to apologize for. As for your plan to sue the commission, well … I actually agree with it.” This made such an enormous change come over her face that I promptly added, “In principle. In reality, it would be very risky.”.

“We don’t have to win the case!”.

“No, that’s not what I mean. It would get press. It could … reignite the opposition to AIO rights as a whole. There are still a lot of BIOs out there who hate and fear the integration. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.
  • According to recent reports, one source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

According to recent reports, one source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are said to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

Van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which demonstrates his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their newly introduced deals.

Alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing matter for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

Industry observers note that it was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

Sources indicate that well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

Slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

He is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner.

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne.

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

In a recent development, the Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Reds hunt for academy recruitment guru.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty.

Confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

It has been revealed that in the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

Fancy running the line, Andoni?

It has been revealed that in the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

It has been revealed that since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Big Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a latest-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool need to see more from their big-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

Bodo/Glimt vs LASK Linz - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Anthony Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 00:01, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 04:43.
  • Hoping to pick up where they left off prior to the international break, LASK Linz will travel to face Bodo/Glimt at Aspmyra Stadion for a Champions League league-phase showdown on Tuesday.
  • Glimt are hoping to climb into the playoff spots, while the Black-Whites are looking to push closer to the top eight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 00:01, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 04:43.

Hoping to pick up where they left off prior to the international break, LASK Linz will travel to face Bodo/Glimt at Aspmyra Stadion for a Champions League league-phase showdown on Tuesday.

Glimt are hoping to climb into the playoff spots, while the Black-Whites are looking to push closer to the top eight.

Kjetil Knutsen's Bodo/Glimt have endured a difficult European campaign to date, winning just one of their four Champions League outings, beating Borussia Dortmund 1-0 in mid-October.

On November 3, Glimt were held to a 0-0 stalemate by Ligue 1's Lille, blanking for the second time in the league phase as part of a concerning trend that has seen the team muster the joint third worst goal tally in the competition, with only PSV and Slovan Bratislava netting fewer than their four.

That frustrating draw has left Knutsen's side 25th in the Champions League table with just four points, though they are level with all of the clubs up to 20th-placed Roma.

Additionally, Bodo/Glimt are a mere two points shy of their opponents, and will be optimistic about their chances of climbing up into one of the playoff qualification spots in midweek.

With that aim in mind, fans of the hosts will be buoyed by their team's record on home turf, where they have lost just one of their 15 outings across all competitions since early May, winning 13 times in the process.

Meanwhile, Dietmar Kuhbauer's LASK kicked off their league phase with two defeats, but have bounced back in impressive fashion to record consecutive wins ahead of Tuesday's clash.

Last time out in the Champions League, the Austrian champions hammered Slovan Bratislava 4-0 in Linz, racing into a 3-0 lead by half time courtesy of a brace from Kasper Jorgensen and a follow-up by Robert Ljubicic.

That victory came as part of a run that has seen Kuhbauer's men net at least four goals in three of their past five matches, and considering they have scored 10 in UEFA's premier club competition, they are likely to pose a threat in midweek.

On the other hand, LASK have conceded nine times across their four Champions League games so far - the joint second worst total in the top 18 - and they will need to be wary of surrendering chances on the road.

The visitors arrive 16th in the table with six points, a tally that puts them two points clear of 25th-placed Bodo/Glimt and three short of eighth-placed Liverpool.

Bodo/Glimt Champions League form:.

Bodo/Glimt form (all competitions):.

LASK Linz Champions League form:.

LASK Linz form (all competitions):.

Bodo/Glimt will be without midfielder Hakon Evjen, who unfortunately suffered further damage to his cruciate ligament while recovering from a previous knee injury, and could reportedly be sidelined for the rest of the season.

In his absence, Patrick Berg, Sondre Fet and Sondre Auklend look set to start in the centre of the park, platforming a front three of Jens Petter Hauge, Ole Didrik Blomberg and Andreas Helmersen, while August Mikkelsen is dealing with a groin issue.

Elsewhere, backup goalkeeper Isak Sjong is a doubt, though Nikita Haikin should be ready to line up between the sticks on Tuesday.

As for LASK, they are missing injured left-back George Bello, so expect to see Yvan Dibango and Kasper Jorgensen operate as wing-backs, either side of a three-man defence featuring Xavier Mbuyamba, Andres Andrade and Alemao.

The visitors also have question marks about the fitness of right-sided attacker Moses Usor, and if he is unavailable, Christoph Lang should join Samuel Adeniran up top in midweek.

Bodo/Glimt possible starting lineup:.

Haikin; Sjovold, Gundersen, Bjortuft, Bjorkan; Berg, Fet, Auklend; Blomberg, Hauge; Helmersen.

LASK Linz possible starting lineup:.

Jungwirth; Mbuyamba, Andrade, Alemao; Bogarde; Jorgensen, Dibango; Ljubicic, Horvath; Lang, Adeniran.

Bodo/Glimt may have found wins hard to come by in the Champions League, but they are unbeaten on home turf in the competition and could prove stubborn opposition once again.

LASK will be confident going forward, though their defensive frailty could cost them at least two points on Tuesday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 00:59.

Liverpool set a upcoming club record in the Premier League for the earliest they have ever taken a 2-0 lead against Manchester United during Sunday's emphatic victory.

The Reds emerged as 4-0 winners against their fierce rivals at Anfield, with the result leaving them fourth in the Premier League table.

Andoni Iraola's side were dominant throughout, though they were aided by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute dismissal for a foul on Alexander Isak outside the box.

That foul led to to Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the subsequent free kick in the 10th minute, before Florian Wirtz netted in the 13th minute.

Opta data reveals that Liverpool have never taken a 2-0 lead against the Red Devils earlier in a Premier League game (12:40), highlighting the impressive nature of the Merseysiders' start.

It has been revealed that 2-0 - This is the earliest that Liverpool have been 2-0 up against Manchester United in a Premier League game (12:40). Relentless. https://t.co/NFFP0MttkL.

The win for Liverpool was significant given it came against the club's biggest rival, but it was also notable for Iraola, who had overseen defeats at home against both Arsenal and Manchester City earlier this season.

Most supporters felt positively about the Basque man, though the lack of a statement victory at Anfield was the only thing missing from his start to life in the dugout.

The Reds experienced numerous low points in 2025-26, with Arne Slot falling out with the crowd on multiple occasions.

If Iraola can quickly endear himself to Anfield and restore the relationship between fans and the dugout, then Liverpool will find it much easier to make their home a fortress once again.

The Reds now trail first-placed Arsenal by seven points, and while it may be too early to consider a title challenge, most fans have started to look at the teams above them rather than those lower in the table.

A seven-point gap is not insurmountable, and if Gunners goalkeeper David Raya is out for a prolonged period, there could be an opening for Iraola's side.

There are still concerns about the Merseysiders in areas like midfield, though a January addition could change the trajectory of the club and push them into contention for a 21st title.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:09 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EST, 18 November 2026.

Leicester have decided to end their deal with controversial sponsors BC.GAME six months ahead of schedule.

Fans expressed fury and dismay earlier this month after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its new ambassador.

Now Leicester have opted to conclude the partnership – in a move welcomed by supporters. A statement on Wednesday read: ‘The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward.

‘We would like to thank BC.GAME for its support throughout its two-and-a-half-year association with Leicester City and for the constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement.

‘Supporters who have purchased a BC.GAME-branded replica shirt through official LCFC retail channels within the last 28 days (since 21 October, 2026) can return it for a full refund or exchange (subject to availability) by Wednesday 2 December.’.

BC.GAME, an online casino company, had been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season. They announced a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this month.

Leicester City have axed a partnership with BC.GAME, after the gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its upcoming ambassador.

Leicester confirmed fans who have purchased a replica shirt featuring the sponsor's name within the last 28 days can return it for a full refund or exchange by December 2.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too.

In recent years, Leicester’s spectacular decline on the pitch has mirrored the relationship with their supporters.

During the years immediately before and after their stunning Premier League triumph in 2016, it was difficult to find a club more in tune with the fanbase.

But a series of baffling decisions – including the tie-up with BC.GAME – eroded trust between the club and their supporters.

Leicester are now in League One and face a long road back but sensible moves like this one suggest they are at least facing in the right direction again.

Sheffield United vs Southampton - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:04, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:15.
  • Separated by just two points in the battle for top-eight places in the Championship table, Sheffield United and Southampton will square off at Bramall Lane on Tuesday.
  • Both teams got back to winning ways in their first game after the international break on Saturday, leaving the hosts ninth and their visitors sixth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:04, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:15.

Separated by just two points in the battle for top-eight places in the Championship table, Sheffield United and Southampton will square off at Bramall Lane on Tuesday.

Both teams got back to winning ways in their first game after the international break on Saturday, leaving the hosts ninth and their visitors sixth.

Sheffield United return to action on Tuesday aiming to make it back-to-back home wins and break into the Championship playoff places.

Aiming to build on 13th-placed finish in 2025-26 and challenge for a Premier League return, the Blades have experienced a mixed start to the season but enjoyed a positive run after the first international break of the campaign, winning four and drawing one of their first six matches October and November, only to go into the November break following a 2-1 away defeat to Charlton Athletic.

That cost the Chris Wilder's side a place in the playoff spots in the second international break of the season, having returned at home to Watford on Saturday with 22 points on the board from their first 15 matches.

The Blades again returned to winning ways in that contest at Bramall Lane, dishing out a 4-0 beating as Ben Brereton Diaz scored a brace inside 20 minutes, Jordan Ayew stretched the lead on the hour mark and Sydie Peck scored a fourth in the 84th minute.

Now sat ninth and just two points behind three teams in the top eight including Saturday's visitors, Sheffield United face another test at Bramall Lane with the hopes of cracking the top eight with a second straight triumph and a third straight home victory.

They face a tough test, though, as the visitors make the long trip north aiming to strengthen their own standing at the top end of the division and increase pressure on the top two with their own second consecutive win.

After only being denied a place in last season's Championship playoff final by the Spygate scandal last season, which also brought about a two-point deduction this term, Southampton have again enjoyed a strong start to the latest term, amassing 29 points from their first 16 matches to sit sixth on 27 points after the deduction.

The Saints have won nine and only lost three of those games, while scoring 31 goals and conceding just 15 - the joint-fewest in the division.

Tonda Eckert's side headed into the November international break on the back of a draw against West Bromwich Albion and a shock defeat to basement team Preston North End, but they bounced back on their return on Saturday, beating Derby County 2-0 thanks to second-half goals from Cyle Larin and Divin Mubama.

That leaves Southampton sixth after 16 matches despite their deduction, two points off fourth spot and five off the top two, and they will look to make it consecutive triumphs in Tuesday's trip to Bramall Lane.

Sheffield United Championship form:.

Sheffield United will remain without Femi Seriki, Matt Doherty, Joe Rothwell and Ryan One due to ongoing injuries, while Kalvin Phillips missed out with a minor glitch at the weekend and may be in contention to return on Tuesday.

They are unable to go unchanged from Saturday's 4-0 win, with attacker Brereton Diaz unable to feature against his parent club while centre-back and captain Japhet Tanganga is suspended for an accumulation of yellow cards.

In his absence, Mark McGuinness will come in to join Liam Kitching at the back, while Patrick Bamford, Tyrese Campbell, Tom Cannon and Jordan Ayew will compete for two attacking spots.

Southampton will head to Bramall Lane without defender Keven Schlotterbeck and midfielder Casper Jander, both of whom are confined to the treatment room, with the former being forced off early in their defeat to Preston before the break.

The Saints could be unchanged from their win at the weekend, with Zach Abbott having deputised at the back in Schlotterbeck's absence, while Leo Scienza also missed out.

Star forward Larin returned to the starting XI on Saturday and scored to make it eight goals in 12 league appearances this season, while Tom Fellows, Finn Azaz and Samuel Edozie will hope to continue in support of the front man despite competition from Kuryu Matsuki, Lewis Dobbin and Divin Mubama.

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:.

Cooper; Choudhury, McGuinness, Kitching, Burrows; Chong, Arblaster, Peck, Donovan; Ayew, Bamford.

Southampton possible starting lineup:.

Peretz; Bree, Stephens, Abbott, Manning; Ward-Prowse, Bragg; Fellows, Azaz, Dobbin; Larin.

Southampton face a tough test in their bid to further ramp up their pursuit of the top two, having fought from behind this season, on Tuesday.

While they boast more quality than the hosts, Sheffield United certainly appear to be growing into the campaign, and we anticipate a share of the points at Bramall Lane.

Quantum physics can prove where you are

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that where you are can matter as much as who you are. Banks, power grids and satellite-navigation systems all depend on knowing where a request or a signal comes from, yet claims about location are notoriously easy to fake. Spoofing and jamming attacks on satellite navigation, for example, are on the rise. Writing in Nature, Kavuri et al.1 report an experiment in which the position of a distant party is certified using the peculiar correlations between quantum particles, known as entanglement. Remarkably, the scheme’s security does not rely on trust of any quantum hardware, only on measurement statistics and the fact that nothing travels faster than light.

#163980. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5908 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most important positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the massive difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Recent findings suggest that zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

It has been revealed that suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

In a recent development, spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Recent findings suggest that asked if Tottenham had made a significant mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi remarked: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he remarked: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Recent findings suggest that jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Recent findings suggest that johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

Sources indicate that “They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery remarked. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

Recent findings suggest that “Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

Industry observers note that “Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

vs Man City (H) - Oct 24th, 12.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia demonstrates his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

Industry observers note that “We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we demonstrated a really good character.”.

Industry observers note that and that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

Late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

This will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

In a recent development, another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Industry observers note that though Savio takes the corner quickly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

It has been revealed that maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

Industry observers note that kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

Sources indicate that but it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

It has been revealed that A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

In a recent development, the Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

In a recent development, gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

Villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

In a recent development, gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

It has been revealed that marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

In a recent development, tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his fresh club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

He gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

So close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

According to recent reports, huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Recent findings suggest that tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

It has been revealed that unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being swiftly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

It has been revealed that savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

Industry observers note that but the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

In a recent development, savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

We’re back in action in north London.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus.

Villa: Wan-Bissaka for Matty Cash.

Sources indicate that and as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

It looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

Possession: Spurs 57% vs 44% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 14 vs 11.

In all fairness to Spurs, they have pushed for a goal all half and only been denied by some fantastic keeping from Zion Suzuki.

Here are some of the biggest saves of the half:.

Industry observers note that predictably, there were boos from the home fans at half-time. That was the ninth half of Premier League football Spurs have failed to score in. They should have done and would have done if it weren’t for the heroics of Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. Manzambi’s goal was only Villa’s second in the League this season and this is the first time they have led in a League game.

Spurs looking shaky now as they come close to conceding a second, seconds before the whistle finally blows.

In a recent development, boos around the stadium as the players head down the tunnel. De Zerbi has work to do.

Spurs have not come from behind to win since November 2024.

This is a tall challenge now, as van Hecke is the first to go into the book for a foul on Jackson.

To rub salt in the wound, Spurs have a decent shout for a free kick on the edge of the box before that as Gomes pushes Mateus Fernandes as he makes a run into the box.

Well this is the last thing Spurs would have wanted. Minutes before half-time Manzambi puts the vistors in front.

Robertson slides to try and stop a ball going out for a corner but he only finds McGinn. He sends it into the box and finds Kamara, who takes a shot. It bounces towards goal and Manzambi pokes it past Kinsky for the lead.

It has been revealed that van de Ven is off the pitch on his feet, sporting an impressive bruise now. Spurs are down to 10 as they try to get the swelling down.

There will be five minutes added, though play is yet to resume as van de Ven receives treatment for a cut below his eye.

The last thing Spurs need now is to be forced into another defensive change after losing Porro.

Wan-Bissaka picks up the ball sent out to him on the wing by Manzambi, who is fouled by Marmoush.

The free kick is outside the area, but McGinn takes looking goalwards.

Mings makes the run looking to get his head on it, but van de Ven goes up with him and gets there first to clear it, though the Dutch international takes a blow to the head and goes down for treatment.

Industry observers note that joao Gomes races forward, sending the ball to Ruggeri on his left. He tries to put it in the box, but it goes out the back off Archie Gray for Villa’s first corner.

Recent findings suggest that mcGinn delivers but it comes off Solanke, who clears. No luck yet as we head towards half-time, despite plenty of action in front of goal.

Roberston again with a sliding cross that Lindelof sends out the back.

Industry observers note that another corner for Spurs, but it is headed away again by Mings, who gets up high. That’s Spurs’s seventh corner.

Great long ball from Robertson to try and find Marmoush but Suzuki comes far outside his area to control it with his chest on the bounce and play it away with his feet.

Recent findings suggest that villa get a free kick inside as Bentancur catches Manzambi, but the Swiss international goes down and receives some treatment on the pitch. He has to go off for a minute, but he is on his feet.

Industry observers note that but Spurs come again and it’s Tonali this time. He takes a shot from outside the area, and would have beaten Suzuki low on the right, but the shot is just wide.

Industry observers note that spurs get a corner, delivered by Savio, and it’s headed on to Solanke at the back post. He heads it towards goal but it’s blocked by Wan-Bissaka. Cries for handball, but it’s cleared.

In a recent development, marmoush makes a very well-timed run to get on a long ball from van Hecke, and does well to stay onside. But his first touch is not good enough and Suzuki can come to collect.

Jackson picks up a ball from Kamara, played over him into the Spurs half. He puts it into the centre of the field towards Buendia, who tees up Manzambi but his shot from distance sails over the bar.

Villa now having a spell. Manzambi gets onto a loose ball in midfield and lays it off to Buendia who feeds Jackson in the centre of the field. He does well to keep the ball down and turn round van Hecke to take a shot on the edge of the area, but he skews his shot wide.

He should be hitting the target at least from there but you can see how desperate both sides are to get their noses in front here.

In a recent development, jackson gets around Gray and runs into the box on the left side. He pokes a ball through to Buendia, who takes a shot on goal at the near post, but Kinsky gets down to his left to stop the shot.

Recent findings suggest that mings almost causes a catastrophe for Villa as he and Lindelof close a loose ball down. Suzuki comes out to claim, but the defender pokes it towards him, almost past him under pressure and the keeper has to send it out the sideline.

Four huge saves by Suzuki as Spurs have had five early shots in total to Villa’s single shot on target. They are finding a lot of joy against the left side of Villa’s defence.

Fernandes has an attempt from distance, but drags his shot wide.

Well Spurs are really pushing for a goal!

It’s a perfect first involvement for Gray, as he times a perfect run to get behind Ruggeri to pick up a ball from Savio. He lets it run inside the box but it flashes across the face of goal, just tipped away by Suzuki.

Another attempt denied immediately after as Savio connects perfectly with the volley on the edge of the area, and Suzuki dives down to his left to parry away.

Incredible start for the Villa keeper and Spurs can smell a goal coming.

Spurs had started on the front foot, but let’s see how they handle this change.

According to recent reports, porro went straight down the tunnel when he went off. It was a problem with his left leg. That’s a blow for Spurs, as Porro offers an attacking threat.

Early concern for Spurs as Porro has gone down and is looking very frustrated. Archie Gray has gone out to warm up, but this is a huge blow for De Zerbi if Porro has to come off.

In a recent development, he had been missing due to a muscle injury but it’s not clear if that’s the matter here. He has been very good so far today, helping build play and bringing huge amounts of experience.

And a shot on target next for Villa as Manzambi has an effort from just inside the 18-yard box off his left foot, but Kinsky makes a relatively easy save as the ball boucnes towards him.

Villa get their first chance, as Jackson races down the left side but van de Ven is content to stay close and as no Villa players follow him into the box, van Hecke is the one who clears his cross into the box.

Suzuki has been good with his feet since joining Villa, but he’s kicked about three balls straight out of play so far today.

No wonder De Zerbi had his t-shirt pulled over his head. Tottenham looked certain to score their first Premier League goal of the season through Savio. Suzuki didn’t know too much about the first shot, which hit him, but reacted well to tip the second over.

Outstanding from the Villa keeper!

Tonali crosses a great ball in from the left and Savio has two great chances from close range but Suzuki blocks the first with his chest and tips the second over the bar.

The corner, delivered by Savio, is headed out by Mings and Villa keep control.

Suzuki plays a long ball out down the field, and as Jackson and van de Ven tussle to reach it, the defender is shoved to the floor and gets the free kick.

Sums up the early battles so far.

Spurs are putting a lot of pressure on Villa as they try and play the ball out, and McGinn loses the ball again in midfield. Spurs surge forward again but Mings gets his head onto the ball crossed into the box and Villa survive again.

According to recent reports, savio takes but it is headed out. It falls to Porro outside the box who lifts another ball in, but the Villa line holds firm and clears for a throw in from the left side.

Marmoush tries to run into the box but a well-time challenge by Kamara gets the ball off him.

It has been revealed that villa lose the ball in midfield and it’s played up to Solanke. Lindelof comes across well but concedes a corner.

And we are underway in north London!

Watch for some long balls from Tyrone Mings down the channels for Nicolas Jackson today. The pair had a little chat before kick-off with Jackson seemingly telling Mings where he wants the ball rolled out to.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Both teams are coming out of the tunnel now, greeted with plenty of noise from the home and away fans.

The stakes are very high for a match so early on the season and kick-off here we come!

This is the second fixture of the week, as Brentford stormed past Chelsea last night 3-0.

Coming up this weekend for you:.

Nottingham Forest vs Coventry (Sat 5.30pm).

Just heard on TNT that Newcastle have won more games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in 2026 than Tottenham have...

An early goal here for Villa could be catastrophic for the home team.

Neither club have had any players called up for England, but plenty of players will be leaving to join up with their national teams abroad.

In a recent development, from Spurs, Pedro Porro has retained his place in Spain’s squad. Both Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke have been called up for the Netherlands and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky will join the Czech Republic squad, still awaiting his first senior cap.

Among the Villa players to receive call-ups, Johan Manzambi will be leaving to join the Switzerland squad, while captain John McGinn has been called up for Scotland once again. Zion Suzuki will leave to join Japan in the three-week break as well.

No Mathys Tel in the Spurs squad. De Zerbi has given him plenty of chances, but Tel has always been one of the first players the head coach has criticised this season.

"I don't see any player that would strike fear into me."Steven Gerrard and Glenn Hoddle give their thoughts on Spurs' transfer business and current squad 💰🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eM22XDDAjs.

“We have to improve in everything, because like I said, after the game we conceded the first goal in a bad way, because we knew what was the initiative in the defensive phase. One long ball on Gakpo is not enough to concede a goal. Also the second goal could have closed Gakpo better and stronger, and the third goal is an individual skill of Szoboszlai.

“We can improve in the qualities of the play. I think we created more chances than the other games, also because Liverpool played with more courage.

According to recent reports, “There was more space to attack, to make one-to-one, but I have experience enough to say that sometimes when you are the coach of the team, without you knowing the reason, you are able to score, you can score. And other times, another situation where I think you are playing well, not fantastic, but well enough to score, enough to win, and you don’t win.

“You have to stay calm, to be confident in what you are doing, what the players are doing. They have my full confidence. We move on and we keep going to be better day by day, but not by words, but by fact.”.

According to recent reports, “Similar, like us, but their potential is a huge potential. They signed, spending, a lot of very good players, but they need as well, time to get compact everything and to achieve understanding their idea.

“Of course, (Roberto) De Zerbi, he’s a fantastic manager. He played fantastic football here and performed fantastic here in Brighton. He did a fantastic job before as well, in Shakhtar, and in Italy, and after Brighton, a fantastic job in Marseille.

“And now, when I can watch them, they are in this process, but of course, they are getting better, they compete fantastic, even losing against Liverpool.

“Of course, being very, very demanding defensively for us, trying to impose and dominate our moment with the ball as well during the game. This is the challenge. Of course, Tottenham, I expect them to be in the top four.”.

Recent findings suggest that two changes for Villa from the side that lost to Nottingham Forest, with Johan Manzambi and Joao Gomes entering the mix. It’s a first full debut for Manzambi since joining the club from Freiburg over the summer. Gomes returns having served his suspension following a red card against Brighton on the opening weekend.

Representing Aston Villa ✊ pic.twitter.com/5xnjiPnRny.

In a recent development, only one change from the team that faced Everton, as Pedro Porro returns to the starting XI, replacing Archie Gray. Carabao Cup goal-scorer Connor Gallagher is on the bench.

Our Spurs side to face Villa 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Xgpl4Hx9VV.

Industry observers note that good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side right now sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Sources indicate that tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

It has been revealed that but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

Stevenage vs Sheffield Wednesday - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:35.
  • In search of a third straight victory with the chance to further narrow their gap to the top two in the League One table, Sheffield Wednesday will head to the SPORTA Arena on Tuesday to take on Stevenage.
  • The visitors have moved to fifth spot and three points behind the automatic promotion places under upcoming management while their hosts sit 14th following a return to winning ways at the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:35.

In search of a third straight victory with the chance to further narrow their gap to the top two in the League One table, Sheffield Wednesday will head to the SPORTA Arena on Tuesday to take on Stevenage.

The visitors have moved to fifth spot and three points behind the automatic promotion places under upcoming management while their hosts sit 14th following a return to winning ways at the weekend.

Stevenage return to action on Tuesday aiming to make it back-to-back victories and finally kickstart their League One season.

After a memorable campaign last time around ended in a sixth-placed finish against the odds on 75 points and eventual playoff defeat, they are yet to truly get going and build on that in 2025-26, having headed into last weekend following the international break on 16 points from 12 league matches.

The last of those matches was a creditable draw against Leicester City, though, before Alex Revell's men recorded consecutive cup victories over Oxford United and Fulham Under-21s and returned to action away at Notts County last weekend.

The Boro would put a fifth three-point haul of the campaign on the board in that contest, as it looked set to end goalless only for Josh Magennis to break the deadlock four minutes from time.

Now sat 14th on 19 points, but just four points off the playoff spots with at least one game in hand on every team above them, Stevenage do have the chance to put themselves in a strong position if they can build on Saturday's win in the next few outings.

That will be no easy task, though, as the visitors arrive aiming to continue a perfect start to life under upcoming management in the league.

Sheffield Wednesday arrived in League One, albeit on the back of relegation and administration last time around, with fresh optimism, a upcoming-look squad and ownership and hopes to bounce back to the second tier at the first time of asking, and after a fast start, manager Henrik Pedersen's tenure would end with consecutive defeats to Notts County and Doncaster Rovers.

A pair of draws followed before the club hierarchy turned to Dave Challinor, whose tenure begun with back-to-back cup defeats to Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley.

It is clear their priorities lie with the league, though, and he has overseen victories in his first two third-tier matches at the helm, as the Owls firstly beat fellow promotion-chasers Plymouth Argyle 3-0 at Hillsborough before visiting Barnsley in a South Yorkshire Derby on Friday and winning 2-1 thanks to Jamal Lowe's first-half brace.

That leaves them fifth with momentum back on their side and just a three-point gap to second spot, and Sheffield Wednesday will now bid to make it three wins in three League One games under Challinor to further ramp up the pressure on the automatic promotion places.

Stevenage form (all competitions):.

Sheffield Wednesday League One form:.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):.

Stevenage will remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts on Tuesday due to ongoing injuries.

Revell should field a similar starting XI from the weekend's away win, although Magennis will likely return from the outset having won that game off the bench with his fourth League One goal of the season having also recorded four assists as their focal point.

He could be joined in a front two by Michael Mellon, who has seven goals in all competitions in the absence of supporting midfielder Kemp, while Louis Thompson and Daniel Phillips will continue their midfield partnership having been regulars this term after several major departures for the Boro over the summer.

Sheffield Wednesday could be unchanged from their victory on Friday, with Reece James, Max Lowe, Tyler Onyango, Mason Burstow and Ali Al-Hamadi likely to miss out again through injury.

Their injury troubles have eased recently, though, with Joe Lumley, Liam Cooper, Di'Shon Bernard, Billy Mitchell and Louie Barry all available after layoffs, and Cooper and Bernard will continue to play in a back three.

The absence of Lowe and James leaves a gap at left wing-back, while forward Jamal Lowe has filled in recent games, netting a brace on Friday, while Barry Bannan and Callum Slattery should again support front man Davis Keillor-Dunn with Barry continuing to be eased back after a lengthy spell in the treatment room.

Stevenage possible starting lineup:.

Setford; James-Wildin, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Sanderson, Thompson, Phillips, Patterson; Mellon, Magennis.

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels, Valery, Heskey, Mitchell, J Lowe; Slattery, Bannan; Keillor-Dunn.

Stevenage head into Tuesday's game in better shape than their league position suggests and are always difficult to beat, having only conceded 13 league goals this term.

Sheffield Wednesday are growing into life under Challinor, though, and are beginning to show the quality that their squad is packed with, particularly with several notable players back to full fitness, and we fancy them to make it three straight wins in a hard-fought away trip.

Latest Update: Vincent Kompany to RETURN to Bayern dugout less than a month after collapsing at training ground: Club chief reveals 'meningeal irritation' has fully 'healed'

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.
  • Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026.

Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.

Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old, who suffered a dislocated shoulder in the fall, underwent tests in hospital which determined that a 'meningeal irritation' had been the cause of his collapse.

Industry observers note that if left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

Kompany was discharged from hospital the following week to continue his recovery at home.

The Belgian coach is now set to return to the dugout when Bayern face Cologne on Friday, with Kompany due to also address the media tomorrow morning.

Vincent Kompany is set to return to the Bayern Munich dugout for their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Kompany's return was officially confirmed by Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen.

Industry observers note that 'Yes, Vincent is in pretty good spirits. I ran into him today,' Dreesen told German outlet Abendzeitung.

Industry observers note that 'The meningeal irritation has healed. He has already undergone shoulder surgery.'.

Kompany had led training for the first time since his collapse earlier this week, with his arm reportedly in a sling following his shoulder injury.

He had missed five matches during his recovery with Bayern winning two and drawing against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

The German champions also beat Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in his absence, as well as progressing in the DFB Cup.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks had overseen the first team during his recovery.

Danks previously worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Kompany has missed five matches following his collapse at Bayern's training ground on October 23.

Bayern had stressed they wanted to give Kompany as much time as required to recover before returning to work.

The German giants play eight matches in the next month, including two matches in the Champions League, before the Bundesliga takes its winter break.

Reports had emerged after Kompany's collapse that club officials had been concerned by his irregular eating habits, as well as barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl dismissed the claims last month, reiterating that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 01:51.
  • Tottenham Hotspur are keeping tabs on Inter Milan striker Francesco Pio Esposito and Porto centre-forward Samu Omorodion, the latest report has claimed.
  • The Londoners continued their strong form on Saturday, emerging as 2-0 winners against Ipswich Town, claiming victory for the fourth time in five top-flight games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 01:51.

Tottenham Hotspur are keeping tabs on Inter Milan striker Francesco Pio Esposito and Porto centre-forward Samu Omorodion, the latest report has claimed.

The Londoners continued their strong form on Saturday, emerging as 2-0 winners against Ipswich Town, claiming victory for the fourth time in five top-flight games.

Roberto De Zerbi's side are now ninth in the Premier League table with 15 points, and there are hope that the team can push for a European spot.

However, it will be a concern to the head coach that his team have only scored 12 goals in their 11 league fixtures.

It comes as no surprise to see Tottenham linked to both Inter's Esposito and Porto's Omorodion by reputable insider szyexcl on X (formerly Twitter), though they add that it is not clear if they will make a move for either player in January.

Esposito has enjoyed a fine season in Italy with Inter, scoring seven goals and providing one assist in just 767 minutes of football in all competitions.

The 21-year-old has proven himself to be deadly in the penalty area, with all six of his goals in Serie A coming from the middle of the box, though he would arguably be reliant on service from Tottenham's creators.

Omorodion has only played 310 minutes for Porto this season, finding the back of the net twice in that time, but there are concerns about how the 22-year-old would adapt to playing at the highest level in England.

While the striker has often performed well in Portugal, the likes of Darwin Nunez and Viktor Gyokeres struggled to bring their best form over to the Premier League, and it would be understandable if figures at Spurs were wary.

The fact that Tottenham are still in a position where they need significant changes in attack is damning given they spent more than £350m in the summer.

Forwards Omar Marmoush and Savio were both signed, but the former has only scored once in the league this season, while the latter is yet to find the back of the net.

Striker Solanke is the team's leading scorer in the top flight with two goals, though it would be wrong to suggest that he has played well this campaign.

Spurs may be in better form, but if they want to sustain a push for a place in Europe, they must strengthen their forward line.
